author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Correct interlaced combing by testing motion and field order
summary: Record a repeatable lateral pan, inspect individual fields, compare supported deinterlacing modes one at a time, and select the mode that removes serrated motion without trading it for bobbing or blur.
heroAlt: PCSX2 split-screen capture used to illustrate video timing and field presentation changes

sourceLabels.pcsx2-q3-2020: PCSX2 notes on frame order and cases that previously required interlacing-mode changes
sourceLabels.pcsx2-writing-patches: PCSX2 documentation for curated no-interlacing patch metadata

blocks.text: Confirm comb teeth exist inside moving frames

Combing appears as alternating horizontal teeth along an object that moves between two captured fields. It differs from vertical jitter, where the whole picture changes position, and from motion blur, where edges remain smooth but leave a temporal trail. Choose a scene with a slow horizontal camera pan past a bright vertical edge, plus a static menu using thin text. Make a direct recording at the device's fixed refresh rate and inspect consecutive frames. Record the game's reported video mode, region, deinterlacing selection, presentation refresh, speed, and any no-interlacing patch.
Do not choose a mode from one paused screenshot. A deinterlacer can make a still frame look sharp while producing reversed cadence, flicker, or doubled motion during play.

items: An in-game save before a ten-second lateral pan that can be repeated at approximately the same speed.
A static screen with one-pixel horizontal details for detecting line loss or bobbing after the motion test.
Native internal resolution, normal emulation speed, post-processing off, and the display locked to a stable refresh mode.
Direct lossless or high-bitrate capture rather than social-media footage with frame blending.
The title's deinterlacing and patch settings written down before any comparison.

blocks.text: Compare cadence without mixing patch and mode changes

items: 1. Cold-boot with automatic deinterlacing, record the pan, and step through frames to locate serrated edges that alternate from one frame to the next.
2. Hold the camera still and inspect menu text; document whether horizontal rows flicker or whether the entire image is already vertically unstable.
3. Cycle to one supported deinterlacing mode, restart the checkpoint, and capture both the moving pan and static detail under that single change.
4. Reject any mode that reverses motion cadence, duplicates contours, throws away obvious vertical detail, or makes the static screen bounce.
5. Repeat the one-mode comparison until one option reconstructs smooth moving edges while retaining acceptable still-image detail.
6. If no mode passes, restore Automatic and check whether the emulator's trusted patch set provides a serial- and CRC-matched no-interlacing patch.
7. Test a matched patch independently from manual mode changes, including menus, FMV, gameplay, and any switch between 480i, 576i, or progressive output.
8. Keep either the chosen deinterlacer or the verified patch route, with its CRC evidence, but do not stack both unless title documentation explicitly requires it.

blocks.text: Interlaced output divides temporal samples into fields containing alternating scan lines. Combining fields from different moments creates comb teeth; displaying each field at a different vertical position can create bob; blending them can reduce teeth while softening motion. Field order and video-mode detection also affect which temporal sample comes first. This is why a controlled clip and static detail are both necessary: the clip grades cadence, while the still section exposes lost line resolution and vertical instability.
The chosen output must pass movement, stillness, mode transitions, and restart behavior.

items: High-contrast moving edges remain continuous rather than breaking into alternating horizontal teeth.
Camera motion advances in the correct direction without two-frame reversals or repeated frames.
Static menu text keeps readable horizontal strokes and does not bounce between line positions.
FMV and gameplay both display correctly when the title changes video mode.
The result repeats after a cold boot at normal speed with no unverified patch active.

blocks.text: Artifacts that are not solved by deinterlacing

items: Smooth edges trail across several frames: disable display motion processing and investigate intentional blur or framebuffer ghosting.
The entire frame shifts even while paused: follow the vertical-jitter workflow instead of cycling more field-weaving choices.
Only a camera recording shows teeth: compare direct capture because rolling shutter and refresh mismatch can fabricate bands.
A no-interlacing patch logs the wrong CRC: disable it immediately; a near-matching regional executable is not valid evidence.

blocks.text: Set deinterlacing to Automatic, disable the tested no-interlacing patch, restore the previous display refresh, and restart from the in-game save. Retain the labeled clips so future emulator builds can be checked against the same pan without relying on memory.
Progressive patches change the game's timing assumptions

A curated no-interlacing patch is executable-specific and can affect presentation or performance beyond the visible scan lines. Verify serial and CRC, read its notes, and never copy a patch between regions merely because the game title is the same.
